reviewed_version: Aalto accepted manuscript arXiv:2108.04421v3, 31 May 2024; selected passages compared with acquired 2025 journal reprint
summary: A nontrivial tying-map fiber is replaced by one term in Lemma 4.5. Exact N=3 meander identities contradict the universal individual collision formula in Theorem 1.2.

problems.claim: For each nonlinked alpha, lim h^(-1/4) Z_alpha = pi Z_tie_remove(alpha).
problems.decisive_evidence: Meander row E gives F_E=Z_B+Z_C. Both B,C tie to a; E removes to b; Z_a=F_b>0. Linked F limit is c=pi Z_a, while the two asserted individual limits would sum to 2c. Exact combinatorial enumeration and rational inverse verified independently.
problems.invalid_step: Last equality in Lemma 4.5 replaces sum over t_j^{-1}(t_j(alpha)) by the alpha term, although the fiber contains B and C in the explicit case.
counterevidence: N=2 fibers can be singleton and do not expose the error
Lemma 4.3 weaker log-normalized vanishing can suffice for linear independence
Theorems 1.3-1.4 are not refuted by this identity; full proofs not certified
problems.correction: For N>=2 and the same admissible collision conditions, the grouped law lim h^(-1/4) sum_{t_j(gamma)=mu} Z_gamma = pi Z_mu for mu in LP_(N-1) follows by grouping before inversion.
problems.correction_limits: The grouped law is restricted to N>=2; the two-point base case is separate. Individual limit values or weights require further analysis. No universal multiplicity correction asserted.
problems.impact: Main Theorem 1.2 individual nonlinked asymptotics and explicit fusion behavior; not a claim of whole-paper failure.
problems.verification_status: Exact finite combinatorics plus analytic inconsistency; matching invalid step actually inspected in journal reprint

independent_verification.result: Confirmed from actual meander definition, linked-F asymptotic and admissible interior collision. E=(16,25,34) has one-loop neighbors exactly B=(12,36,45) and C=(14,23,56), so F_E=Z_B+Z_C. Both tie at j3 to a=(12,34), whereas E removes to b=(14,23); the N2 meander matrix gives Z_a=F_b. At y=(-2,-1,1,2), B.2 yields pi^2(8/9)^(1/4) hypergeom(1/2,1/2;1;8/9)>0. The linked law gives c, the two disputed individual laws give 2c. Grouping first and inverting the lower-order matrix yields the repair for N>=2 without assuming individual limits. Same invalid last equality was read in retained journal p66.

clarifications.evidence: Z=F=pi h^(1/4); logarithmic normalization gives zero.
clarifications.scope: Section 4.2 assumes N>=2. Theorem's N>=1 and endpoint notation need explicit base convention; not used to establish P1.

limitations: No full independent certification of Sections 2-3 and Appendices C-D
No separate correction identified in bounded search, not proof of absence
